questions.subject: Climate Change / Ecology
questions.passage_text: Scientists studied the vernal window — transition period from winter to the growing season. They found that warmer winters with less snow resulted in a longer lag time between spring events and a more protracted vernal window. This change in the spring timetable has ecological, social and economic consequences — for agriculture, fisheries and tourism. As the ice melts earlier, the birds don’t return, causing a delay or lengthening in springtime ecological events.
questions.question_text:
With reference to the above passage, the following assumptions have been made:
1. Global warming is causing spring to come early and for longer durations.
2. Early spring and longer period of spring is not good for bird populations.
Which of the above assumptions is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

questions.passage_text: A global analysis of nitrogen use efficiency shows that excessive fertilizer use increases pollution of waterways and air. Only 40% of nitrogen applied to cropland is used by crops, while the rest is lost to the environment, causing nitrous oxide emissions and eutrophication of water bodies.
